note:
Malcolm's revision of the pile: he likes the stack of box packaging, but wants them stacked properly rather than leaning, each carton the correct size, and the labelling correct. Just the four cream cartons.

THE FIX FOR THE GARBLED TEXT. PILE1 produced 'CLUTATHIONE', 'PRO COLAGEN', 'SLUTTHIONE RIGHITTERING' and a mirrored wordmark, because the brief asked for label text without saying what to do with the lines it did not name — so the model set every remaining line as type and invented the words. The per-product packaging specs already solve this: they instruct that side-panel copy be rendered as 'fine unreadable print, never as placeholder words'. That instruction is applied here to EVERY line below the named headlines, on every face. The failure mode becomes illegible fine print, which is what small print actually looks like, instead of misspelled brand copy.

CORRECT SIZE. All four are the same 50ml squat format — wide and short, broader than tall — so they are the same size as each other. Stating that explicitly is checkable; 'correct size' is not.

COLOUR. Two of the four are steel blue, so the night cream is turned to its silver alternate face to keep four distinct colours in the stack: pink, steel blue, silver, teal.

CLASS A throughout, reference-locked to approved packshots. The night cream reference comes from the 2026-08-20 run rather than publish-ready, because no carton shot of it was ever published — only jar shots.

slots.title: Four cream cartons squarely stacked, graphite ground
slots.prompt: Studio photograph of exactly four Skingenetix cream cartons from the reference images, stacked squarely one on top of another into a single neat upright column in the centre of a tall portrait frame. All four cartons are identical in size and shape - the same wide, short rectangular 50ml format, broader than it is tall, with crisp square edges and a luxury matte-metallic satin finish. They sit flat and level on each other, front faces flush and aligned, edges parallel, no carton tilted or leaning, the column standing straight and stable. From top to bottom: the soft dusty pink PDRN carton, then the medium steel blue Copper Peptide day carton, then the brushed pale silver face of the Copper Peptide night carton, then the deep emerald-teal Matrixyl carton at the base. The stack is photographed slightly from the front and just above eye level of the top box so the front faces are square to camera and a sliver of each lid surface shows. Legible type, and nothing else, reads on the front faces: on the pink carton the Skingenetix DNA-helix mark with the wordmark 'Skingenetix', then 'PDRN COLLAGEN REPAIR', then 'DEEP RENEWAL TREATMENT'. On the steel blue carton the same mark and wordmark, then 'COPPER PEPTIDE', then 'ADVANCED DAY REPAIR'. On the silver carton the same mark and wordmark, then 'COPPER PEPTIDE', then 'ADVANCED NIGHT REPAIR'. On the teal carton the same mark and wordmark, then 'MATRIXYL 3000', then 'PRO COLLAGEN'. Every remaining line on every face is fine print far too small to read - render it as fine unreadable print, never as placeholder words, never as invented wording, and print nothing that is not quoted here. A single hard key light from the upper left with one soft fill, throwing one clean defined shadow of the whole column down and to the right across a smooth seamless graphite surface, colour #1A1A1A, that fills the background evenly. Premium skincare campaign still life, crisp focus across the front faces, physically based matte cardboard.
